userStories.title: Move run temp roots under /tmp/nax with per-user fallback
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Move sanitized session temp directories into run-owned roots under /tmp/nax (or a per-user fallback), preserve run-scoped cleanup and exclude nax's temp trees from tmpWrite telemetry.

**Motivation** — A flat `/tmp/nax-<runId>` root is hard to find and list. A single `/tmp/nax/` parent is easier to inspect, but a shared parent created by one OS user is not writable by another, so it needs a fallback.

**Approach** — **Temp root layout (US-001).** `runTmpRoot` resolves the parent on every call. That's a few
synchronous `lstat`/`access` calls through an injectable `_sessionTmpDeps`
(`{ lstat, access, uid }`), and there is no cache.

1. `lstat("/tmp/nax")` fails with ENOENT: the parent is `/tmp/nax`. `mkdir -p` in the launcher
   creates it with the default mode.
2. `lstat` reports a directory (not a symlink), and `access(W_OK | X_OK)` succeeds: the parent is
   `/tmp/nax`.
3. Otherwise the parent is `/tmp/nax-<uid>`, where `<uid>` is `process.getuid()`. The otherwise
   case covers: a symlink, a regular file, `access` failing, or `lstat` failing with anything
   other than ENOENT.

The wipe removes `runTmpRoot(runId)` only, never the parent, so concurrent runs under
`/tmp/nax/` are untouched.

**Scope** — In: update session-tmp, its sandbox barrel export, run-only wipe expectations and tmpWrite exclusions for both `/tmp` and `/private/tmp`; update existing tests that pin the flat path. Out: sandbox policy selection/configuration (US-002) and agent-facing descriptions (US-003). Windows and any platform without `process.getuid` — `/tmp` paths already assume POSIX. A `/tmp/nax-*` or `/tmp/nax/*` sweep of stale directories from crashed runs — the wipe stays run-scoped. The command-safety question set, model, labels and the `outside_project` rule regexes — the rule scorer never matches `/tmp`, so no rule change is needed. Making `/tmp/nax` world-writable (mode 1777) — the per-user fallback covers multi-user hosts instead.

**Interface** — `_sessionTmpDeps` — new in `src/sandbox/session-tmp.ts`, re-exported from `src/sandbox/index.ts`. Shape: `{ lstat(path): { isDirectory(): boolean; isSymbolicLink(): boolean }, access(path, mode): void, uid(): number }`, synchronous and throw-based like `lstatSync` / `accessSync`; production values are `lstatSync`, `accessSync` and `process.getuid`.
`runTmpRoot(runId: string): string` — `src/sandbox/session-tmp.ts`. Target: returns `<parent>/<sanitized runId>`, where `<parent>` is `/tmp/nax` when that path is absent or is a real directory writable by the current user, and `/tmp/nax-<uid>` otherwise. `sessionTmpDir(runId, sessionName)` is `runTmpRoot(runId)/<sanitized sessionName>`, with sanitization unchanged. `detectTmpWrite(command, cwd?)` also excludes paths under `<root>/nax/`, for both `/tmp` and `/private/tmp`.

When _sessionTmpDeps.lstat reports /tmp/nax is a symbolic link, _sessionTmpDeps.access succeeds, and _sessionTmpDeps.uid returns 501, then runTmpRoot("run-1") returns /tmp/nax-501/run-1.

userStories.title: Confine available sandbox temp writes to run root by default
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Confine available sandbox launchers with a run ID to the run's temp root by default while preserving shared-root opt-out, no-run fallback, and safe mkdir failure fallback.

**Motivation** — The sandbox grants the whole of `/tmp`: `defaultTempRoots()` returns `[os.tmpdir(), "/tmp"]` (`src/sandbox/policy-inputs.ts:70`) and `buildSandboxPolicy` adds every temp root to `writeRoots` (`src/sandbox/policy-builder.ts:120`).

**Approach** — **Temp roots (US-002).** In `resolveSessionSandbox`:

- `config.filesystem.allowSharedTmp` is true, or `args.runTmpRoot` is undefined: the temp roots
  are `_sessionSandboxDeps.tempRoots()` (today's call, still `defaultTempRoots` in production, so
  `test/integration/sandbox/sandbox-live.test.ts` keeps its stub) and the state omits `sharedTmp`.
- Otherwise, create `args.tmpDir` with `_sessionSandboxDeps.mkdir` before building the policy.
  - Creation fails: log `warn` (stage `sandbox`) and use `_sessionSandboxDeps.tempRoots()`; the
    state omits `sharedTmp`.
  - Creation succeeds: use `_sessionSandboxDeps.runTempRoots({ runTmpRoot, tmpdir: _sessionSandboxDeps.tmpdir() })`,
    and the state carries `sharedTmp: false`.

`runTempRoots` returns `[runTmpRoot]`, prefixed by `tmpdir` only when `tmpdir` is neither `/tmp`,
`/private/tmp`, nor under either. On Linux, `os.tmpdir()` is usually `/tmp`, and keeping it would
re-grant all of `/tmp`. The darwin `/tmp/claude` root that srt needs stays, because
`buildSandboxPolicy` adds it independently of `tempRoots`.

**Scope** — In: schema allowSharedTmp default false, runTempRoots, optional available-state sharedTmp, injectable mkdir/tmpdir/runTempRoots, policy selection, dispatch propagation of runTmpRoot, and unit/live sandbox tests. Out: layout and fallback selection implementation (US-001) and agent-facing wording (US-003). Rewriting agent commands to replace `/tmp` paths — nax never edits agent-authored commands. The unsandboxed path (sandbox disabled or unavailable): writes to `/tmp` stay allowed there; only the prompt text applies.

**Interface** — `defaultTempRoots(): string[]` stays the shared-tmp roots; add `runTempRoots(opts: { runTmpRoot: string; tmpdir: string }): string[]` next to it. `_sessionSandboxDeps` gains `mkdir`, `tmpdir` (`() => os.tmpdir()`) and `runTempRoots`, so `resolveSessionSandbox` makes no un-injected external read. `resolveSessionSandbox(args)` gains `readonly runTmpRoot?: string`, supplied by `resolveDispatchLauncher(options, declared, sessionName)` as `runTmpRoot(options.runId)` whenever it supplies `tmpDir`. `SandboxState` available variant gains OPTIONAL `readonly sharedTmp?: boolean`: absent means shared temp roots (today's behaviour), so every existing construction of the variant stays valid. `SandboxConfigSchema.filesystem` gains `allowSharedTmp: z.boolean().default(false)`. Policy writeRoots compare via `realOrRaw(...)` on macOS because `/tmp/...` realpaths as `/private/tmp/...`. Do not change the launcher’s existing TMPDIR export or the independently added darwin `/tmp/claude` root.

userStories.title: Tell agents to use scratchpad and confined TMPDIR
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Describe confined temp roots accurately in Bash/Exec tools, append temp guidance on sandbox denials, and name the scratchpad as the agent's temp folder.

**Motivation** — The scratchpad prompt section describes `.nax/scratchpad/` only as a place for notes and snippet scripts. It is the one temp location that every tool can reach (shell, Read/Write/Edit, and the Scratchpad tools), but the prompt never calls it a temp folder.

**Approach** — **Agent-facing text (US-003).** Exact strings:

- `sandboxSentence(network, false)` replaces "the system temp directories" with "this run's temp
  directory ($TMPDIR)". `sandboxSentence(network, true)` returns today's text unchanged.
- `denialHintLine(writeRoots)` appends: ` For temporary files use $TMPDIR or .nax/scratchpad/, not /tmp.`
- `buildScratchpadSection()` replaces the paragraph beginning "Shell commands run with `$TMPDIR`"
  with:

```
Use the scratchpad as your temp folder. Files you make while working — command output you want to
re-read, generated inputs, one-off scripts — go under `.nax/scratchpad/`: the shell, the file tools
and the scratchpad tools can all reach it, and it is cleared after the run. For throwaway files a
command creates on its own, shell commands run with `$TMPDIR` set to this run's temp directory; use
`$TMPDIR` or `mktemp` for those. Never write to `/tmp` directly: in the sandbox, `/tmp` outside
`$TMPDIR` is not writable and the write fails.
```

**Scope** — In: update sandbox messages, the three available-state Bash/Exec sentence call sites, the scratchpad paragraph, related existing assertions and only the affected snapshot text. Out: changing actual sandbox roots (US-002) and renaming temp roots (US-001). Rewriting agent commands to replace `/tmp` paths — nax never edits agent-authored commands. The unsandboxed path (sandbox disabled or unavailable): writes to `/tmp` stay allowed there; only the prompt text applies.

**Interface** — `sandboxSentence(network, sharedTmp = true)`; single-argument calls keep today's text. Callers `src/tools/bash.ts:188,203` and `src/tools/run-command.ts:263` pass `state.sharedTmp !== false`. `denialHintLine(writeRoots)` appends the exact temp-folder sentence. `buildScratchpadSection()` replaces the `$TMPDIR` paragraph only, preserving the rest of the scratchpad lifecycle guidance. Available-state `sharedTmp: false` (from US-002) triggers the confined wording; omitted sharedTmp retains legacy wording.
acceptanceCriteria: sandboxSentence("open", false) returns a sentence that names this run's temp directory ($TMPDIR) as a writable root in place of the system temp directories.
sandboxSentence("open", true) returns the pre-change sentence for network "open".
sandboxSentence("open") returns the pre-change sentence for network "open".

Given a launcher whose available state is { kind: "available", backend: "srt", network: "open", sharedTmp: false }, when the Bash tool description is built, then it contains this run's temp directory ($TMPDIR).
Given an available state with sharedTmp: false, when the run-command tool description is built, then it contains this run's temp directory ($TMPDIR).

analysis: Goal: replace instruction-only TMPDIR isolation with default sandbox-enforced per-run temp write roots, retaining explicitly opted-in shared temp and fail-open behavior when the session temp directory cannot be created. Architecture: src/sandbox/session-tmp.ts:16-30 currently sanitizes each run/session part using /[^A-Za-z0-9_-]/g -> '_' and puts sessions under /tmp/nax-<runId>; expose synchronous, mutable _sessionTmpDeps for lstat/access/getuid and resolve /tmp/nax on every call, falling back to /tmp/nax-<uid> for non-directory, symlink, inaccessible or non-ENOENT errors. src/sandbox/index.ts:29 exports runTmpRoot/sessionTmpDir and should export the new seam and runTempRoots. src/execution/lifecycle/run-tmp-wipe.ts:27-49 already removes exactly runTmpRoot(runId), force-recursive, warns and swallows removal errors; preserve run-only cleanup and update obsolete layout comments/test. src/command-safety/tmp-write.ts:15-74 uses a lexer and normalized POSIX paths for redirects and write-target commands; current nax- prefix exclusion must also exclude /tmp/nax/ and /private/tmp/nax/ without excluding /tmp/naxfoo. This is a telemetry signal, not a command refusal. src/sandbox/policy-inputs.ts:70-72 provides the legacy defaultTempRoots of os.tmpdir() plus /tmp; add runTempRoots alongside it, excluding os.tmpdir when /tmp or /private/tmp or descendants, retaining other os tmpdirs. src/agents/coding-tool-support-resolve.ts:18,364-380 is the dispatch seam already passing sessionTmpDir only when options.runId exists; pass runTmpRoot under that same condition. src/agents/coding-tool-sandbox.ts:28-106 has the injectable _sessionSandboxDeps and async resolveSessionSandbox: only the enabled, probed-available, needsLauncher branch builds a policy, currently calling tempRoots() per policy build; create tmpDir before the first policy build and select confined roots or fall back to tempRoots on mkdir failure; inject mkdir, tmpdir and runTempRoots to avoid uninjected reads. Existing disabled/unavailable branches continue exporting TMPDIR without confinement. src/sandbox/launcher.ts:73-84,157-179 independently mkdir-p's tmpDir before each command and exports TMPDIR/TMP/TEMP (wrapped commands get shell export); do not change launcher semantics. src/sandbox/policy-builder.ts:115-141 puts tempRoots into writeRoots, realpath-normalizes paths with literal()/realOrRaw(), and independently allows /tmp/claude on darwin; tests must compare realOrRaw(path). src/sandbox/types.ts:47-50 available state should gain optional sharedTmp=false only for confinement; omitted must retain old constructor/equality behavior. src/config/schemas-sandbox.ts:23-40 uses zod 4 prefault({}) so the added allowSharedTmp=false gets populated for {} and nested filesystem {}; old full-object schema tests require updated expectations. src/sandbox/messages.ts:15-38 houses reusable sandboxSentence/denialHintLine; src/tools/bash.ts:183-203 uses sentence in raw and gated/escalate descriptions, src/tools/run-command.ts:261-266 uses it for Exec descriptions, so pass sharedTmp !== false at all three sites. src/prompts/sections/scratchpad.ts:29-51 provides unconditional scratchpad instructions; replace only the old TMPDIR paragraph with the exact prescribed wording while retaining the separate failed-run retention text.
